newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas- Taiwan, Saudi direction sought.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas- Taiwan, Saudi direction sought.

text.p: Activity on the light distillates market was largely stymied on Monday as traders waited for further direction from Saudi Aramco for naphtha and Taiwan for gasoline.
Naphtha buyers remained on the sidelines as further development on the Saudi Aramco term talks was awaited.

Term talks for the second half of the year's liftings had reached a deadlock on Friday with endusers unwilling to raise bids to meet Aramco's target offer of $15 per tonne premium for its full range naphtha.
Singapore swaps firmed with crude, with June discussed at $22.10/$22.20 per barrel, up from $21.75/$22.00 on Friday.
"Prices are still firm on the absolute," a trader said about the spot market. "The arbitrage looks attractive but no exports (from the Mediterranean) have been fixed yet."
Trade on Singapore naphtha barrels lifting in June has been thin with only one cargo heard sold at around 45 cents per barrel over spot quotes, by a U.s. major, traders said.
In the gasoline market, the Japanese trader actively buying cargoes last week, bought 50,000 barrels of 92-octane at $23.45 per barrel fob Singapore, lifting June 11-15 from a Dutch trader.

The level was little changed from the trader's two purchases of the same grade for June 5-9 and June 8-12 loading at $23.60 and $23.30 respectively, as traders focussed on Taiwan's 95-octane unleaded reformate tender which closes late Monday.
Taiwan is seeking its third 250,000-barrel cargo for June 11-30 and one for July 1-15 delivery.
Traders said with the rise in crude, they expected the award to be higher than the last two cargoes purchased at $25.30 per barrel c-and-f Taiwan June 11-30.
"It could be higher," said one trader. "It depends on who is desperate to sell."

Traders assessed the market long to balanced with stocks in Singapore at a two-year high at around 7.6 million barrels, with a further half a million Thai barrels lifting this week and early June heading to Singapore, adding to previous imports from Australia.
But on the bullish side, high domestic demand in China is expected to dry up exports in June, they said.
(Prices are in dollars per barrel)
